cityWatch.label: CITY WATCH
cityWatch.text: BMTC’s minimum ordinary-bus fare has risen from ₹6 to ₹10, a 67% increase for the shortest rides, effective today.

lead.headline: BMTC MINIMUM FARE JUMPS 67% AS KARNATAKA BUS HIKE KICKS IN
lead.deck: The city’s ordinary-bus minimum rises from ₹6 to ₹10; BMTC fares increase 33–35% on average
paragraphs: Higher bus fares take effect across Karnataka from Thursday, with Bengaluru commuters facing the steepest average increase. The minimum fare on an ordinary BMTC service, for a ride up to two kilometres, rises from ₹6 to ₹10; the maximum rises from ₹35 to ₹45.

The transport department estimates an average increase of 33–35% for BMTC and 23% for the other state-run corporations. The government says the revision is intended to shore up the transport undertakings amid rising operating costs and losses.
For frequent riders, the change adds to household travel costs from today. Officials said revised fares apply across BMTC, KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC services.

sidebarStory.headline: AGNIVEERS OFFERED TWO-YEAR SERVICE EXTENSION
sidebarStory.subhead: The new option takes the engagement to six years for those not selected for regular service
paragraphs: The Union Cabinet has approved an additional two-year engagement for Agniveers who are not absorbed into the regular armed forces after four years. The change gives the remaining 75% of each cohort a chance to continue for a second tour, while the existing 25% selection for regular service remains. The first batch was due to complete its initial tenure in December 2026.

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru city, civic, and court news

stories.headline: CITY TO CENTRALISE BULK-WASTE COLLECTION
paragraphs: Bengaluru Solid Waste Management plans to take over bulk-waste collection and route it to empanelled processors, according to a report published Thursday. The change would place collection and processing under a citywide system.

stories.headline: HIGH COURT QUASHES FIR OVER SLOGAN AT BJP PROTEST
paragraphs: The Karnataka High Court quashed a case against BJP protesters accused of raising a pro-Pakistan slogan. The court said the allegation appeared improbable and accepted the explanation that the words were a slip of the tongue.

stories.headline: CM URGES PRIVATE SCHOOLS TO PARTNER WITH RURAL GOVERNMENT SCHOOLS
paragraphs: Karnataka has signed 15 memoranda with private schools to support 56 government schools, with an initial target of 1,000 partnerships and an eventual goal of 2,000. The programme is intended to improve facilities and learning in rural schools.

groups.ariaLabel: India courts, economy, and diplomacy news

stories.headline: STATES CAN LEVY ADDITIONAL SALES TAX UNDER PRE-GST LAWS: SC
paragraphs: A seven-judge Constitution Bench upheld states’ authority under pre-GST laws to impose an additional sales tax or surcharge. The ruling concerns the earlier tax regime; the reference has limited practical reach after GST came into force in 2017.

stories.headline: US SANCTIONS INDIA-BASED FIRMS OVER ALLEGED IRAN OIL LINKS
paragraphs: The United States announced sanctions on entities and individuals based in India and Turkey, alleging they supported an Iranian oil network. The allegations are Washington’s; the affected parties’ responses should be checked in subsequent reporting.

stories.headline: OCTOBER SERVICES GROWTH HITS FOUR-MONTH HIGH
paragraphs: New orders and resilient demand lifted India’s services activity in October to its strongest pace in four months, according to the latest purchasing managers’ survey. The expansion points to continued momentum in a large, employment-intensive part of the economy.

groups.ariaLabel: Karnataka schools, families, and sport news

stories.headline: PRESCHOOL BODY WARNS 25,000 CENTRES COULD FACE CLOSURE
paragraphs: A Karnataka preschool association has sought a review of operating norms, warning that about 25,000 standalone centres and the livelihoods of 4.5 lakh women could be affected. The figures are the association’s estimates; it is urging the state to reconsider the rules.

stories.headline: BESCOM VERIFICATION FLAGS 1.42 LAKH GRUHA JYOTHI ACCOUNTS
paragraphs: A verification exercise has flagged 1.42 lakh of the scheme’s 74 lakh consumers as not yet verified, raising the possibility that some could lose the free-electricity benefit. The government has not announced a final decision; affected users should await official guidance.

stories.headline: KARNATAKA THUMP ASSAM BY AN INNINGS AND 314 RUNS
paragraphs: Karnataka completed a dominant Ranji Trophy win over Assam by an innings and 314 runs. Manvanth Kumar remained unbeaten on 100 while K V Aneesh made 145 in Karnataka’s commanding performance.

groups.ariaLabel: India cricket, air quality, and Bengaluru weather

stories.headline: DELHI AQI 377; FORECAST WARNS OF SEVERE AIR ON FRIDAY
paragraphs: Delhi’s average air quality reached 377 on Wednesday, its worst reading in nearly ten months, while 22 monitoring stations recorded severe levels. Forecasters expect very poor air on Thursday and a possible move into the severe category on November 6–7; authorities have stepped up action against crop-residue burning.

stories.headline: IMD EXPECTS CLOUD AND LIGHT RAIN IN BENGALURU
paragraphs: The IMD forecast generally cloudy skies and light rain in Bengaluru for Thursday, with a thunderstorm and lightning warning in the city forecast. The published city outlook gives temperatures around 21–29°C.
